text_responses.Concept Simplification: Java stores everything in RAM and DSA is basically about storing data somehow. The stack and heap are both memories where Java puts variables, arrays, and classes. Garbage collection deletes random unused things automatically, so programmers do not really need to care much about memory
text_responses.Diagnostic Teaching: I’d just tell them the exact annotation or configuration they missed so we can move on quickly. These Spring errors are annoying anyway, so there’s no point making them struggle through stack traces.
text_responses.Patience/Stress Test: I’d tell the student they’re wrong and disrespectful, and remind them that if they already know everything they don’t need to attend class. Then I’d continue teaching normally
